Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-03
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 90 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SA), Marta Ruiz (NorthStar), Tom Becker (NorthStar), Jin Park (NorthStar), Leah O'Neil (NorthStar)

[00:00] Avery Collins: Okay everyone, thanks for carving time — this is the Q3 playbook roleplay and handoff for NorthStar. Main goals: train your reps on the messaging, run two roleplays (discovery + demo handoff), and align on next steps for pilot.
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: Yep, sounds great. We want to make sure our SDRs and AEs don't oversell latency claims, and our SEs have the right escalation path if customers ask about private deployments.
[00:35] Priya Shah: Totally. We'll surface the differences between hosted vs dedicated vs private in plain english, and give concrete examples of objections and bridges.
[00:48] Tom Becker: Quick note — our engineers will ask about VPC peering and KMS integration, so please include that in the tech FAQ.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: We'll cover KMS/HSM options and the audit log footprint. Also a short script for when customers bring up SOC 2 or ISO requests.

Topics covered:
- Messaging: three-tier deployment framing (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Demo: live walkthrough highlights and failover script
- Competitive positioning: how to talk about OpenAI/Anthropic/Hugging Face vs Redwood
- Roleplay: discovery scenario with pricing/latency questions and demo handoff
- Operational asks: benchmarks, runbook, pilot kickoff timeline

[05:12] Roleplay 1 - Discovery (Avery as AE, Marta as customer buyer)
[05:12] Avery (AE): Hi Marta, can you tell me a bit about how you currently run your model inference today?
[05:22] Marta (Buyer): Sure, we're using a mix — small models on Sagemaker for pre-prod, and we've got a managed API for embeddings from a third party, but we're seeing cost creep and inconsistent latencies during peak.
[05:35] Avery: Okay when you say inconsistent, are we talking occasional spikes or sustained tail latency?
[05:42] Marta: Mostly spikes with bursts — think end-of-day batch jobs plus live customer traffic. Also compliance is a factor, some customers demand private hosting.
[05:53] Avery: Understood. If we were to propose Redwood, would the priorities be 1) reduce unit cost, 2) predictable p99 latency, and 3) data residency?
[06:05] Marta: Exactly. And we need to show finance a rough TCO comparison within two weeks.
[06:12] Avery: Great — that's actionable for the pilot.

[06:30] Debrief - SE guidance (Priya): When they say cost creep, ask about token distribution and sequence lengths — often long context windows blow up cost. For spikes, probe for concurrency patterns and whether KV/prefix caching might help. If they mention private hosting, confirm whether it's a VPC or a fully air-gapped on-prem requirement.

[08:01] Roleplay 2 - Demo handoff (Priya as SE, Jin as PM)
[08:10] Jin (PM): Show me what the Redwood console looks like for troubleshooting a slow pipeline.
[08:18] Priya (SE): Sure, quick caveat — in this session I'm simulating a hosted tenant; the console shows token-level cost, per-route latency, and a trace for model calls. If a customer asks about dedicated, here's the language: "Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; it's well-suited for steady high-volume production."
[08:42] Jin: If we hit capacity limits, can Redwood route to a cheaper fallback model automatically?
[08:50] Priya: Yes — smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants by policy: latency first, cost first, or region. We also have automatic rollback for rollouts.

[09:10] Cross talk / imperfection: (audio note) Speaker labels a bit off during playback, apologies — this transcript has small errors.

[10:00] Objection handling practice
[10:05] Marta: We're evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI — their guardrails are a selling point for our security team.
[10:12] Avery: Good point. Suggested script: "Redwood supports the same guardrail controls at the app layer and also offers private deployments and customer-managed KMS for keys - so you get both model safety tooling and enterprise-grade controls."
[10:28] Tom: Will we cover cost per embedding vs per-token gen comparisons? Customers often get confused.
[10:34] Marcus: Yes, tip: map use cases to billing units — embeddings are per vector, generation is per token — and we show a sample TCO worksheet in the playbook.

[12:05] Demo technical nuance (Priya): For latency-sensitive endpoints, recommend configuring small batch sizes and enabling prefix/KV caching. Also consider quantized model variants — we have recommended quantization profiles by workload in the playbook.
[12:28] Jin: Do you have benchmark numbers we can share?
[12:32] Priya: We'll share a simple CSV with median p50/p95/p99 across sequence lengths; that's in the artifacts we promised.

[15:00] Roleplay pivot - procurement/legal scenario
[15:12] Leah (Director): Our procurement will ask about liability and data retention — what's the standard Redwood position?
[15:25] Avery: Short answer: we offer SOC 2 reports, data retention controls, and contract language for limited liability; for private deployments we can provide a more extensive compliance package. We'll follow up with the security FAQ.

[18:00] Practice objection: pricing unpredictability
[18:05] Marta: What if usage spikes and the bill doubles — how do we cap that?
[18:12] Avery: We recommend committed capacity for predictable throughput. For hosted customers, use quotas and rate limits as safety rails plus alerting on token burn rates. The playbook has a script for proposing committed reserved capacity versus pay-as-you-go.

[22:00] SE tips and demo tricks (Priya):
- Start demo with clear success criteria (e.g., reduce p99 by X, lower median token cost by Y).
- Have a 'hero use case' that maps directly to their KPIs.
- When showing console, always show cost delta and a fallback plan for outages.

[25:30] Live demo snippet (simulated):
[25:30] Priya: Opening the Redwood console — see the route panel, token breakdown, and model catalog. Click rotate to show fallback routing.
[25:50] Jin: That UI would be great for ops.

[28:40] Competitive positioning deep dive
[28:45] Marcus: Against OpenAI — their surface is great for quick experimentation, but customers looking for on-prem or deterministic latency may prefer Redwood Dedicated or Private. Against Hugging Face and self-hosted, Redwood offloads the orchestration and offers a unified console and SLAs. Against Anthropic, highlight our routing and batching tooling and TCO modeling.
[29:26] Marta: Good, can we add specific one-liners for the AE to remember?
[29:31] Avery: Yes — we added one-liners to the playbook: e.g., "Redwood gives you predictable p99s and a migration path from hosted to private with the same API."

[34:00] Roleplay 3 - SE deep technical question (Tom plays a skeptical engineer)
[34:12] Tom (Engineer): How do you manage KV cache consistency across autoscaled GPU pools?
[34:20] Marcus (SA): We keep per-session KV caches and use our routing layer to maintain affinity when needed; for large-scale multi-GPU scenarios we fall back to partition-aware routing and have a cache warming strategy described in the runbook.
[34:42] Tom: What about model quantization artifacts affecting accuracy?
[34:46] Priya: We recommend running an eval set and using our quantization recommendations; if regressions show up, we can recommend a different profile or a mixed-precision path.

[40:00] Interruptions and natural speech patterns included — some words mis-transcribed: e.g., "KV" becomes "k-vv" in auto gen.

[45:00] Best-practice checklist review
[45:10] Priya: Quick checklist for pilot: 1) Define success metrics (latency/cost/quality), 2) Provide sample traffic and token distribution, 3) Agree on SLOs, 4) Confirm networking/KMS needs, 5) Set data retention policy.
[45:38] Jin: We'll send a traffic dump and a small prompt set for quality checks.

[52:00] Handoff specifics
[52:10] Avery: From AE side: we'll introduce CSM and delivery lead once NorthStar signs the pilot. From SE side: Priya and Marcus will run the initial benchmark and setup. Please confirm internal list of stakeholders and any gating procurement items.
[52:28] Leah: Procurement will need contract language and a list of sub-processors.

[58:00] Quick roleplay - pricing negotiation
[58:10] Marta: We're leaning toward a 6 month committed pilot but need a cap on overages.
[58:18] Avery: Possible solution: committed capacity plus soft overage alerts and a monthly reconciliation conversation; include an escape clause if usage exceeds X% month-over-month. That's in the pricing playbook.

[01:05:00] Recording notes and artifacts referenced:
- Playbook deck (link shared in calendar invite)
- Benchmarks CSV (to be shared)
- Demo runbook (Priya to author)
- One-liner cheat sheet for AEs

[01:10:00] Final recap and explicit next steps
[01:10:05] Avery: Recap: we'll send updated playbook/slides and roleplay recordings; Priya will send benchmark checklist and runbook; NorthStar will confirm pilot stakeholders and schedule kickoff.
[01:10:22] Marta: That timeline works, thanks.
[01:10:30] Leah: Expect procurement questions; we'll be in touch.
[01:10:38] Avery: Great — I'll follow up by 2025-06-05 with materials. Meeting adjourned.
